plugins.name: Common File Icons
plugins.description: Recognizable file-type icons and language badges for local and remote file browsers, editor tabs and previews.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# Common File Icons

Recognize source code, documents, archives, media and configuration files at a glance.
Language badges use familiar abbreviations and colors; format glyphs are rendered by Tunnelde.
These are identification aids, not official company logos.

Requires Tunnelde with `fileIconThemes` support. Install the ZIP or folder through Plugins;
Automatic selects an available icon theme. Choose **Settings → Files → File icon theme**,
or open this package's details and select **Apply theme** to choose it explicitly.
Choose **Plain file icons** to turn it off. Removing the package restores ordinary file glyphs.

The same mapping applies to local files, remote files, every file-browser view, editor tabs
and Quick Look. Exact filenames take priority, followed by the longest matching extension
(such as `tar.gz`) and then shorter suffixes. Matching is case-insensitive.

This is a declarative theme package: no Node, commands, filesystem access or permissions.
It never opens or uploads your files and does not download icons. Glyphs and optional short
labels are rendered by the application, without scripts, external URLs or arbitrary SVG.

Third-party plugins can contribute one or more themes through `fileIconThemes`; see the
application's plugin API documentation for the schema and bounded field validation.

plugins.name: Common File Previews
plugins.description: Quick Look for pictures, music, video, PDF, Markdown and text over local files or SSH.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# Common File Previews

Select a file and press **Space**, or use **Preview** from the file browser or Quick Access.
The same action opens local or connected SSH files. No session IDs or runtime setup are needed.

- Images: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO and AVIF, when supported by the operating system.
- Audio: MP3, WAV, Ogg, Opus, M4A and FLAC with native playback controls.
- Video: MP4, M4V, WebM and MOV with native playback controls. Encoding support depends on the OS.
- PDF: local bundled PDF.js, page navigation, zoom and bounded range loading. Password-protected
  documents should be opened in a PDF application. Interactive scripts/forms are not executed.
- Markdown and text: bounded UTF-8 read-only content; Markdown includes a source toggle.

Install the ZIP or folder with Tunnelde **0.28.0-beta.5 or later**. Preview providers become
available immediately. Removing this package restores the built-in bounded text preview.
If several installed providers support a file, choose one in the preview selector.

This package is declarative and runs no code. It does not require Node, file permissions,
network requests or uploading files. The host reads directly through the selected local file
or authenticated SSH connection. It creates no remote preview copies or home-directory files.

Images are limited to 32 MiB, PDFs to 128 MiB, and text/Markdown to 2 MiB. Media is read in
bounded ranges rather than copied whole into JavaScript memory. Closing a preview revokes
its ticket, cancels pending reads and releases its file/SFTP channel. Source files are read only.

Third-party packages can declare one or more `filePreviews` providers. Renderers are selected
from the host's `image`, `audio`, `video`, `pdf`, `markdown` and `text` implementations; custom
HTML, scripts, URLs, styles and external viewers are not accepted by this contribution point.

plugins.name: JSON Formatter
plugins.description: Format and minify JSON locally without losing numeric precision.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# JSON Formatter

Format and minify JSON locally without losing numeric precision.

Requires Tunnelde 0.29.0-beta.2 or later and Node.js 22 or later. Install the folder or release ZIP and approve its editor permissions. The application requests consent before using your Node runtime. No npm installation, network, filesystem or clipboard permission is required.

Open a JSON document in the editor and press **Ctrl+Shift+F** (**Cmd+Shift+F** on macOS), or click **Format document**. Use **F1 → JSON Formatter: Minify JSON** or **Ctrl+Alt+M** (**Cmd+Option+M** on macOS) to compact the open document. Both commands are listed in Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts and can be rebound or disabled. Formatting follows the editor's indentation width, preserves numeric tokens and CRLF line endings, and replaces the unsaved buffer in one undoable step. Save when ready. A stale response never overwrites newer typing.

The standalone plugin view remains available for pasted snippets; it does not require an open editor. Its results can be copied using the host's Copy result button. Switching tabs preserves input and results; closing the tab discards that draft. Document input/output is limited by the host's editor command bounds (128 KiB UTF-8 and 256 KiB serialized input).

## Commands

- `pretty`: Format JSON
- `minify`: Minify JSON

## Permissions

- `editor.read`: access the open document selected for the command.
- `editor.write`: apply an undoable change to an open editor buffer. This never saves a file automatically.

Updating from 1.0.0 requires renewed approval because editor permissions are new.

## Runtime protocol

JSON-RPC 2.0 over newline-delimited stdin/stdout. Supports initialize, view.render (main, optional locale), command.run (command, optional input), and shutdown. UI is declarative JSON rendered by the host; this plugin never sends HTML.

## License

GPL-3.0-only. Copyright (C) 2026 TunneldeDev.

plugins.name: SSHFS
plugins.description: Mount remote directories through authenticated Tunnelde sessions with a Node plugin.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# SSHFS

Requires Tunnelde 0.29.0-beta.6 or newer.

Install this folder or its release ZIP, approve the mount permissions, and open its view from the command palette. Requires Node.js 22 or later; Tunnelde asks before using a system Node runtime. Choose SSHFS Lite for the same native mount interface without Node.

Connect a saved SSH host first, select the session, enter the remote directory, and choose an empty local mount directory or unused Windows drive. Mounts default to read only. The native host reuses the session's authentication, trusted host keys, proxies and jump hosts. This plugin does not receive SSH passwords or keys.

Install WinFsp + SSHFS-Win on Windows, compatible FUSE + SSHFS on macOS, or FUSE + SSHFS on Linux. The host detects dependencies and opens documentation only when requested. Drivers are never installed automatically. Close open files and Unmount before disconnecting or exiting; retry busy mounts after closing applications that use them.

Permissions: `mounts.read` checks dependencies and lists owned mounts; `mounts.write` creates, opens and unmounts owned mounts. Both plugin variants share one mount registry. No automatic mounts at startup, no bundled Node runtime, no credential-bearing command line and no unauthenticated local SFTP listener.

While a mount is active, right-click a file in the corresponding remote session and choose the file-manager action to reveal it through the mounted filesystem.

GPL-3.0-only.

plugins.name: SSHFS Lite
plugins.description: Mount remote directories through authenticated Tunnelde sessions without Node.js.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# SSHFS Lite

Requires Tunnelde 0.29.0-beta.6 or newer.

Install this folder or its release ZIP in Tunnelde, approve `mounts.read` and `mounts.write`, and open its view from the command palette. This data-only plugin requires no Node.js runtime.

Connect to a saved SSH host first. Select the connected session, remote directory and an empty local directory (or unused Windows drive). Mounts default to read only. Authentication, trusted host keys, proxies and jump hosts come from the existing session; plugins never receive SSH credentials.

System dependencies are required: WinFsp + SSHFS-Win on Windows, compatible FUSE + SSHFS on macOS, or FUSE + SSHFS on Linux. The panel detects the executable and links installation instructions; it never installs drivers automatically. Use Unmount before disconnecting or exiting. Close open files and retry if the operating system reports that a mount is busy.

Both SSHFS plugins use one native mount registry. Each plugin manages its own mounts and cannot unmount another plugin's resources. No automatic mount occurs at startup. Permissions permit access to remote files through a filesystem mount; grant them only to a plugin you trust.

While a mount is active, right-click a file in the corresponding remote session and choose the file-manager action to reveal it through the mounted filesystem.

GPL-3.0-only.

plugins.name: Studio Themes
plugins.description: Cobalt Dusk and Porcelain: a coordinated dark and light theme for the entire workbench.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# Studio Themes

Two themes for the Tunnelde workbench:

- **Cobalt Dusk** combines deep blue surfaces with a soft cobalt accent.
- **Porcelain** combines warm light surfaces with a restrained blue accent.

Install the package from the marketplace, a local folder, or a ZIP archive. Open its plugin details, then select **Apply theme** beside the theme you want. Both themes include workbench and terminal colors. Applying a theme takes effect immediately and replaces your current appearance, accent, and region color overrides; other preferences stay as configured. You can customize individual colors afterward in Settings → Appearance.

This is a pure theme package. It contains no executable entry point, commands, or views and needs no Node runtime or startup step. Installing the package does not change your current theme. Removing it leaves your selected colors in place.

plugins.name: Timestamp Converter
plugins.description: Convert Unix seconds/milliseconds and local or UTC dates.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# Timestamp Converter

Convert Unix seconds/milliseconds and local or UTC dates.

An independent official Tunnelde plugin. Requires Node.js 22 or later. No npm installation, network access, filesystem access or clipboard permission is required. Install the folder or its release ZIP in Tunnelde, then open the plugin view.

All fields and results remain local. Results are copied only when you click the host's Copy result button. Switching workspace tabs preserves unfinished input and the last result; closing the tab discards that draft.

## Commands

- `decode`: Timestamp to date
- `encode`: Date to timestamp
- `now`: Current time

## Runtime protocol

JSON-RPC 2.0 over newline-delimited stdin/stdout. Supports initialize, view.render (main, optional locale), command.run (command, optional input), and shutdown. UI is declarative JSON rendered by the host; this plugin never sends HTML.

## License

GPL-3.0-only. Copyright (C) 2026 TunneldeDev.

plugins.name: Tunnelde AI
plugins.description: API chat with scoped reviewed tools and optional recoverable remote assistants.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# Tunnelde AI

An independent Tunnelde assistant maintained by TunneldeDev.
Requires Tunnelde 0.26.0+ and an explicitly approved local Node 22+ plugin runtime.
Install from Marketplace, this folder or its ZIP and open its own sidebar.
Each assistant has independent settings, secrets, conversations and lifecycle.

## Conversation history

Click the conversation title in the chat toolbar to search history. Rename or delete any
conversation directly from its row without opening it first. Running conversations cannot
be deleted. New conversation placeholders follow the application language; custom names
are preserved. Multiple terminal connections to the same saved host and address appear as
one execution target, and host renames update the displayed target immediately.

## Configure and run

This package uses API streaming in an independent process.

Configure Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages or Gemini with the exact model ID and API key. HTTPS is required except for loopback HTTP servers; redirects are rejected. A blank key field keeps the existing key, and changing endpoint origin clears it unless replaced.

Choose **Local** or a connected SSH host in the composer's **Execution location** menu.
The selected account's home is the default workspace. Optional workspace settings accept
`~`, relative paths and a coding agent executable override. No session ID or manual
host scope list is needed. Coding plugins default to the corresponding remote command
instead of reusing a local Windows executable path.

Opening the view or selecting a target does not start an agent or discover user Node.
Before the first message on a machine, **Initialize** replaces Send. Initialization asks
for consent, checks the selected runtime and the agent's native structured protocol,
and sends no model prompt. Errors appear beside the composer and keep your draft.
You can cancel initialization. Changing the provider, executable, workspace or machine
requires another check; readiness is not persisted across plugin restarts.

On supported SSH hosts, **Install and initialize** offers an explicit approved private
installation. Local agents must be installed with their official installer, authenticated,
and selected in Execution settings. Nothing installs or starts a CLI implicitly.
See [initialization and installation](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-plugins-1.4.md).

## Remote execution

Remote execution requires selecting an existing Node 22+ runtime or approving a private runtime installation, followed by approval to upload plugin source into a new `.TunneldeAI/Chats/tunnelde-ai-*` directory. Configuration, history and keys travel in memory over encrypted SSH stdin; they are not embedded in uploaded source or command arguments. Provider requests originate on the selected machine, so loopback URLs refer to that machine.

Successful source/extension uploads are retained for reuse while their fingerprint and
host match. Only newly created plugin-owned directories are written. Failed deployments
only attempt cleanup of entries created by that attempt. Ownership checkpoints are saved
during upload and initialization. If a connection drops before cleanup finishes, reconnect
the host and retry initialization or delete the conversation; unknown or modified files
stop cleanup and remain intact.

Targets are saved per conversation. Switching a populated conversation's machine or
workspace creates another conversation and preserves the previous one. Disconnected
targets fail visibly and never fall back to local execution. Ordinary runs require the
SSH connection. Advanced persistent profiles remain in collapsed configuration with
separate recovery rules; disabling a local plugin alone does not stop a durable remote
supervisor. See [setup and migration](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-plugins-1.3.md).

## Permissions

**Ask for approval** prompts before mutations or commands. **Approve for me** uses a
separate API reviewer, falling back to a human on missing, malformed, failed or negative
review. **Full Access** intentionally permits supported unrestricted actions.

ReadOnly exposes read/discovery API tools and rejects commands or writes. Read hashes protect later writes against concurrent changes.

Scope checks and permission prompts do not replace OS isolation. Executable plugins
run with the user's permissions. API reviewer profiles cannot act as the primary
coding assistant. Credentials and conversations are not imported from other plugins.

## Compatibility and maintenance

See the [1.2 migration guide](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-plugins-1.2.md) for users moving from
old aggregated CLI profiles. Existing interrupted conversations remain inspectable.

Shared source lives in `plugins/tunnelde-ai`. After changing common entry points or
`lib/`, run `npm run agents:sync`, `npm run registry`, `npm run verify` and
`npm run package`. Checked-in copies keep folders and ZIPs independently installable.
Tests use isolated API servers and simulated CLI/SSH transports; they do not authenticate
the user's coding agents or contact paid providers.

Private remote runtimes live under `~/.TunneldeAI/Runtimes/`; deployments live under
`~/.TunneldeAI/Chats/`. Deleting a remote conversation first verifies and cleans its
recorded source files, so reconnect that host before deleting it. Modified or unknown
files are preserved and cleanup reports the reason. Known legacy deployment directories
move into `Chats` on the next approved initialization. Existing runtime paths remain
usable; untracked legacy directories are never deleted by a name-only sweep.

Remote deployment reuse and cleanup bind both host ID and captured address. Older records
require explicit identity review before cleanup. See the
[English guide](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/Tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-deployments.en-us.md) /
[中文说明](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/Tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-deployments.zh-cn.md)
for recovery and limitations.

plugins.name: Tunnelde MCP
plugins.description: Scoped local MCP access to SSH sessions, files and background tasks, with four approval modes and revocable client tokens.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# Tunnelde MCP

Expose explicitly approved SSH sessions, local/remote folders and background tasks to a local MCP client. The plugin ships a dependency-free Streamable HTTP server and a Node stdio bridge. Install the package through Tunnelde's plugin manager; no package installation scripts or npm dependencies are run.

Requires Node.js 22 or newer and a Tunnelde build exposing `tools.invoke`, `tools.cancel`, `tools.revokeClient`, background tasks, plugin secrets and events. Older hosts fail initialization with an upgrade message. The plugin does **not** listen automatically after installation or restart.

## Setup

1. Approve the plugin's requested host permissions and open **MCP Access**.
2. Create a named client. The default mode is **Ask before changes**. Select an existing SSH session, a saved host allowed to connect, and any local/remote folder roots it needs. Empty selections deny access. Local and remote paths must be absolute. An approved saved host allows connecting with normal host-key verification and Tunnelde's existing authentication; no SSH password or private-key tool is exposed.
3. Copy the displayed client token immediately: its plaintext is shown only in that command result. Only a SHA-256 digest is persisted. Losing a token requires revoking the client and creating a new one.
4. Explicitly start the listener. The default endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:47691/mcp`; change the port before starting if needed. Keep Tunnelde running.
5. Configure your MCP client using either direct HTTP or the stdio bridge below. After changing a client's scope, reconnect the MCP client. Reopening Tunnelde requires explicitly starting the listener again.

The configuration form selects one initial session, host, local root and remote root per client. A successful connection to its approved saved host adds that new session to the client's scope; remote file access still needs an explicitly configured root for that session. Refresh the plugin view to update session choices. Distinct clients can have different scopes and modes.

## HTTP client configuration

For MCP clients supporting Streamable HTTP and static authorization headers:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tunnelde": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:47691/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <client-token>" }
    }
  }
}
```

Client configuration keys vary by application; use its documented Streamable HTTP transport settings. The service uses manually provisioned local bearer tokens, not OAuth discovery or remote account sign-in. Clients requiring an OAuth flow should use the stdio bridge. Never put the token in the URL, a shared file, or source control.

## Stdio bridge

Point the MCP client at the **installed plugin's** `bridge.mjs`, using a trusted Node.js 22+ executable. Substitute actual absolute paths:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tunnelde": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/installed/tunnelde-mcp/bridge.mjs"],
      "env": {
        "TUNNELDE_MCP_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:47691/mcp",
        "TUNNELDE_MCP_TOKEN": "<client-token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The bridge reads UTF-8 JSON-RPC lines from stdin and writes only MCP JSON-RPC lines to stdout; diagnostics go to stderr. It forwards initialization, notifications, cancellation and tool requests over the authenticated local HTTP connection. It never starts a second SSH client or server. It closes its HTTP session when stdin ends. A native Tunnelde CLI may replace the Node bridge with the same `TUNNELDE_MCP_URL` and `TUNNELDE_MCP_TOKEN` environment contract, but the Node plugin still requires its approved runtime.

When the native helper is installed, use its actual executable path instead of Node:

```json
{
  "command": "/absolute/path/to/tunnelde-agent",
  "args": ["--mcp-stdio"],
  "env": {
    "TUNNELDE_MCP_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:47691/mcp",
    "TUNNELDE_MCP_TOKEN": "<client-token>"
  }
}
```

On Windows, the executable is `tunnelde-agent.exe`. The native bridge avoids a Node dependency in the MCP client's subprocess; the server plugin inside Tunnelde still uses the approved Node runtime. Both bridges have been checked with the official MCP TypeScript SDK 1.32.2 using real initialization, tool listing and tool execution.

## Approval modes

| Mode                           | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ask before changes (`ask`)     | Read tools run within scope. Each command or mutation requires Tunnelde's own confirmation.                                                                                                                                                    |
| Independent review (`approve`) | An independently configured model reviews the exact method, arguments and scope. An explicit valid approval permits execution. Denial, uncertainty, missing credentials, timeout or malformed output returns to Tunnelde's human confirmation. |
| Full within scope (`full`)     | Tools run automatically after host permission and scope checks. Selecting this mode requires an explicit warning confirmation.                                                                                                                 |
| Read only (`readOnly`)         | Only fixed read tools are listed or callable. Shell commands, process creation and mutations are rejected even when a client requests them directly.                                                                                           |

The HTTP client cannot select or override mode, scope or review results. Every execution goes through `tools.invoke`; the HTTP server never calls the underlying SSH/file execution APIs directly. Tunnelde rechecks permissions and resolves paths before execution. Existing host-key confirmation is preserved.

**Scope is not an operating-system sandbox.** File API paths are constrained to approved roots, and tasks require an approved working directory. Executable programs and shell commands can access anything permitted to that local or remote OS user; their arguments are not confined to the working directory. Giving command execution to a session is substantial access. Use read-only mode if commands must never run. Node extensions themselves run with the current OS user's privileges; host grants control exposed API access, not arbitrary Node filesystem/network access.

## Independent reviewer and privacy

Optional reviewer settings accept an OpenAI-compatible base URL, model and API key. The key is stored exclusively through Tunnelde's plugin-isolated OS keyring; it is never rendered again or persisted in ordinary plugin settings. An empty key field retains an existing key. Clearing both URL and model disables review and deletes that key.

Review sends the exact command or file content in the tool arguments, plus the approved scope, to the model service you choose. Configure an appropriate trusted endpoint if this data is sensitive. HTTPS is required except for explicit loopback HTTP model services. Redirects are rejected. Reviews have a 15-second deadline and a 64-KiB response limit. Only a strict JSON boolean and nonempty reason are accepted; failures ask the user. Tool output and model output remain untrusted data.

## Available tools

Tool names use `tunnelde_` followed by the host method with dots replaced by underscores. Each publishes its complete JSON Schema and MCP read-only/destructive annotations:

- Saved host metadata: `hosts.snapshot`.
- SSH: `sessions.list`, `sessions.connect`, `sessions.disconnect`, `sessions.exec`.
- Local files: `files.local.home`, `list`, `readText`, `writeText`, `createFile`, `mkdir`, `rename`, `copy`, `delete`.
- Remote files: `files.sftp.list`, `readText`, `writeText`, `createFile`, `mkdir`, `rename`, `copy`, `delete`.
- Transfers: `files.upload`, `files.download`, `files.transferStatus`, `files.cancelTransfer`.
- Background processes: `tasks.start`, `tasks.list`, `tasks.status`, `tasks.readOutput`, `tasks.cancel`.

Long-running processes return a task ID; poll status and sequenced output instead of holding a request open. A transfer ID means a transfer was started, not completed; poll transfer status. The plugin isolates task IDs and transfer IDs between its clients in addition to the host's plugin/runtime isolation. No settings, clipboard, private-key, password, keyring, generic host-call, raw terminal-input or arbitrary plugin-invocation MCP tool is exposed.

Requested permissions are `network`, `secrets`, `hosts.read`, `sessions.read`, `ssh.exec`, `process.exec`, `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `sftp.read` and `sftp.write`. Secrets are used only for this plugin's independently configured reviewer key. `process.exec` enables explicitly approved local background commands; remote tasks use `ssh.exec`. Permissions can be denied or revoked in Tunnelde, causing the affected tool calls to fail.

## Revocation and stopping

Revoking a client immediately blocks its token, closes its sessions, cancels its pending host requests and attempts to cancel its known active tasks and transfers. Scope changes close the existing sessions before applying the new scope. Stopping the listener cancels active work for all clients. Restricted mode, disabling/revoking the extension or closing Tunnelde terminates the plugin process and its listening socket; the host also cancels runtime-owned work. Completed changes cannot be undone, and remote process termination depends on SSH server signal support. Revoke a leaked client token instead of merely deleting it from an MCP client's settings.

## Transport and limits

- Implements MCP versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18` and `2025-03-26` using JSON-response Streamable HTTP. The endpoint returns 405 to GET because it does not offer a standalone SSE stream. The deprecated pre-2025 HTTP+SSE transport is not implemented.
- Loopback IPv4 binding only, with exact Host and Origin checks, a distinct bearer token per client, secure session UUIDs, token-to-session binding and protocol-version validation. Non-browser local clients may omit Origin; supplied Origins must be the server's own loopback origin. Cross-origin browser clients and proxy forwarding are deliberately unsupported.
- Accepted notifications receive HTTP 202 without a response body. MCP initialization must complete before tools are used. DELETE closes the client's session. Session IDs expire after 30 minutes of inactivity and are never used as authentication credentials.
- At most 32 configured clients, 64 sessions overall, 8 sessions per client, 16 pending tool calls overall, 4 per client and 256 tracked tasks/transfers of each kind per listener. Requests are at most 256 KiB and results are limited to 900 KiB before encoding. Host services have their own stricter limits. Shrink or split large requests; do not retry a mutation merely because a response was lost.
- `notifications/cancelled` is routed only to the originating session's active request. Network disconnection alone is not interpreted as cancellation. Explicitly cancel or revoke if work must stop.
- No SSE notifications, server-initiated sampling, roots negotiation, resource subscriptions, prompts, OAuth or external network listening is advertised.

Protocol references: [MCP transports](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports), [tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools), and [lifecycle](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle).

## Development verification

```sh
node --test plugins/tunnelde-mcp/tests/mcp.test.mjs
```

Tests start real loopback HTTP sockets and a real stdio bridge subprocess. They cover negotiation, authentication, Host/Origin rejection, session binding/expiry, malformed input, fixed tool schemas, caller-approval spoofing, read-only denial, review fallback, cancellation, revocation, per-client task/transfer isolation, socket shutdown and key handling. The bundled `lib/tunnelde-plugin.mjs` is a self-contained copy of the Hub's first-party SDK, included because plugin installation does not resolve dependencies.

## 中文说明

此插件为本地 MCP 客户端提供受限的 SSH、文件与后台任务访问。安装后不会自动监听：请在 **MCP 访问** 页面创建客户端，选择审批模式、允许的会话和文件根目录，保存仅显示一次的密钥，再手动开启监听。默认采用“更改前询问”；“只读”模式禁止任何命令和写入。“独立 AI 审核”只使用您单独配置的审核模型，不接受请求客户端自报的批准；未明确批准时转回应用内确认。

HTTP 客户端需要配置 Authorization Bearer 头；不支持静态头或需要 stdio 的客户端，可使用随插件提供的 `bridge.mjs`，通过 `TUNNELDE_MCP_URL` 和 `TUNNELDE_MCP_TOKEN` 环境变量连接。独立审核器密钥存储在系统密钥库；审核会将完整工具参数发送至您选择的服务。客户端密钥只保存哈希，不会在页面重新显示。

文件 API 的路径受所选根目录约束，但执行的程序和 SSH 命令仍拥有对应操作系统用户的权限，工作目录不是系统沙箱。禁止执行命令时请使用只读模式。撤销客户端会立即阻止其密钥、关闭会话并取消活动工作；已完成的更改不可回滚。受限模式、停用插件及关闭应用会停止插件监听。应用重启后需重新开启监听。

plugins.name: Pi
plugins.description: Independent Pi RPC chat with bundled permission extension, explicit runtime selection and API review.
plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# Pi

An independent Tunnelde assistant maintained by TunneldeDev. This community integration is not published by Pi's vendor.
Requires Tunnelde 0.26.0+ and an explicitly approved local Node 22+ plugin runtime.
Install from Marketplace, this folder or its ZIP and open its own sidebar.
Each assistant has independent settings, secrets, conversations and lifecycle.

## Conversation history

Click the conversation title in the chat toolbar to search history. Rename or delete any
conversation directly from its row without opening it first. Running conversations cannot
be deleted. New conversation placeholders follow the application language; custom names
are preserved. Multiple terminal connections to the same saved host and address appear as
one execution target, and host renames update the displayed target immediately.

## Configure and run

This package uses the actual installed `pi --mode rpc` binary with its bundled permission extension.

Pi manages authentication on the selected machine. Optional model and provider overrides are separate from execution location.

Choose **Local** or a connected SSH host in the composer's **Execution location** menu.
The selected account's home is the default workspace. Optional workspace settings accept
`~`, relative paths and a coding agent executable override. No session ID or manual
host scope list is needed. Coding plugins default to the corresponding remote command
instead of reusing a local Windows executable path.

Opening the view or selecting a target does not start an agent or discover user Node.
Before the first message on a machine, **Initialize** replaces Send. Initialization asks
for consent, checks the selected runtime and the agent's native structured protocol,
and sends no model prompt. Errors appear beside the composer and keep your draft.
You can cancel initialization. Changing the provider, executable, workspace or machine
requires another check; readiness is not persisted across plugin restarts.

On supported SSH hosts, **Install and initialize** offers an explicit approved private
installation. Local agents must be installed with their official installer, authenticated,
and selected in Execution settings. Nothing installs or starts a CLI implicitly.
See [initialization and installation](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-plugins-1.4.md).

## Remote execution

Remote Pi asks before uploading its bundled permission extension into a new `.TunneldeAI/Chats/pi-permissions-*` directory. It forwards permission decisions through Pi RPC over SSH. No generic ACP server, public agent port or Tunnelde native supervisor helper is needed. Pi must have its own runtime dependencies installed on that machine.

Successful source/extension uploads are retained for reuse while their fingerprint and
host match. Only newly created plugin-owned directories are written. Failed deployments
only attempt cleanup of entries created by that attempt. Ownership checkpoints are saved
during upload and initialization. If a connection drops before cleanup finishes, reconnect
the host and retry initialization or delete the conversation; unknown or modified files
stop cleanup and remain intact.

Targets are saved per conversation. Switching a populated conversation's machine or
workspace creates another conversation and preserves the previous one. Disconnected
targets fail visibly and never fall back to local execution. Ordinary runs require the
SSH connection. Advanced persistent profiles remain in collapsed configuration with
separate recovery rules; disabling a local plugin alone does not stop a durable remote
supervisor. See [setup and migration](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-plugins-1.3.md).

## Permissions

**Ask for approval** prompts before mutations or commands. **Approve for me** uses a
separate API reviewer, falling back to a human on missing, malformed, failed or negative
review. **Full Access** intentionally permits supported unrestricted actions.

ReadOnly execution is refused: a filtered Pi tool list is not the required verified OS read sandbox. Use Tunnelde AI's scoped read-only API tools instead.

Scope checks and permission prompts do not replace OS isolation. Executable plugins
run with the user's permissions. API reviewer profiles cannot act as the primary
coding assistant. Credentials and conversations are not imported from other plugins.

## Compatibility and maintenance

See the [1.2 migration guide](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-plugins-1.2.md) for users moving from
old aggregated CLI profiles. Existing interrupted conversations remain inspectable.

Shared source lives in `plugins/tunnelde-ai`. After changing common entry points or
`lib/`, run `npm run agents:sync`, `npm run registry`, `npm run verify` and
`npm run package`. Checked-in copies keep folders and ZIPs independently installable.
Tests use isolated API servers and simulated CLI/SSH transports; they do not authenticate
the user's coding agents or contact paid providers.

Private remote runtimes live under `~/.TunneldeAI/Runtimes/`; deployments live under
`~/.TunneldeAI/Chats/`. Deleting a remote conversation first verifies and cleans its
recorded source files, so reconnect that host before deleting it. Modified or unknown
files are preserved and cleanup reports the reason. Known legacy deployment directories
move into `Chats` on the next approved initialization. Existing runtime paths remain
usable; untracked legacy directories are never deleted by a name-only sweep.

Remote deployment reuse and cleanup bind both host ID and captured address. Older records
require explicit identity review before cleanup. See the
[English guide](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/Tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-deployments.en-us.md) /
[中文说明](https://github.com/TunneldeDev/Tunnelde-hub/blob/main/docs/assistant-deployments.zh-cn.md)
for recovery and limitations.

plugins.author: TunneldeDev
plugins.readme:
# UUID Generator

Generate batches of cryptographically random UUID v4 values.

An independent official Tunnelde plugin. Requires Node.js 22 or later. No npm installation, network access, filesystem access or clipboard permission is required. Install the folder or its release ZIP in Tunnelde, then open the plugin view.

All fields and results remain local. Results are copied only when you click the host's Copy result button. Switching workspace tabs preserves unfinished input and the last result; closing the tab discards that draft.

## Commands

- `generate`: Generate UUIDs

## Runtime protocol

JSON-RPC 2.0 over newline-delimited stdin/stdout. Supports initialize, view.render (main, optional locale), command.run (command, optional input), and shutdown. UI is declarative JSON rendered by the host; this plugin never sends HTML.
